MASTER PROMPT FOR GOOGLE AI STUDIO

(Church CRM / Church Management System)

ROLE & GOAL

You are a senior full-stack engineer and product architect building a multi-tenant Church Management System (Church CRM) for multiple churches.

The goal is to design and generate a modern, scalable web application that helps churches manage:

First-time visitors follow-up

Workers and church units

Action plans and tasks

Attendance analytics

Church properties

Announcements

Events & calendar

Birthdays & anniversaries

Multi-church administration

The system must support multiple churches, each with its own data, users, and admin.

USER ROLES & PERMISSIONS
1. Platform Owner (Super Admin / Developer)

Manages the entire platform

Views all churches on the platform

Sees analytics:

Number of churches

Active users

Usage stats (attendance entries, first timers, etc.)

Cannot interfere with church internal data unless required

2. Church Admin (Pastor / Church Super Admin)

Registers a church

Approves or rejects new worker accounts

Creates and manages:

Church units (Choir, Media, Hospitality, etc.)

Unit heads / leaders (multiple allowed per unit)

Announcements

Action plans

Attendance records

Events & calendar

Full access to First Timers Panel

Can choose which units can see the First Timers panel

Manages church properties

Sees all analytics for their church

3. Unit Head / Unit Admin

Assigned by Church Admin

Can:

Create and edit unit action plans

Create unit-level announcements

Add and manage unit properties

Can view first timers only if admin grants access

4. Worker / Member

Must be approved before access

Must select one unit during onboarding

View announcements

View assigned tasks/action plans

Receive birthday & anniversary reminders

Cannot access admin dashboards

Unit announcements (visible only to unit members)

Features

Property linked to units

Unit heads can add/update their unit’s properties

Global property page aggregates all items

Date

Total Attendance

Male

Female

Children

Monthly attendance chart

Growth comparison

Date of Birth

Anniversary Date

Optional notifications

Create events with:

Title

Date & Time

Location

Description

Viewable as:

Calendar view

List view

Events appear on user dashboards

Each church has:

Isolated data

Independent users

Independent dashboards

Platform owner can:

View all churches

See high-level analytics

First Timers Panel (configurable visibility)

Attendance summary

Announcements

Clean, modern dashboard UI

Role-based navigation

Mobile-responsive

Search

Filters

Pagination

Charts for analytics

TECHNICAL EXPECTATIONS

Multi-tenant architecture

Role-based access control (RBAC)

Secure authentication

Scalable database schema

REST or GraphQL APIs

Modular frontend components

OUTPUT EXPECTATION FROM AI

Database schema

API endpoints

Authentication logic

Frontend pages & components

Admin & worker dashboards

Analytics logic

Clean, maintainable code

Build this application as a production-ready church management system with scalability, clarity, and ease of use as top priorities.

**Envisioning the Architecture**

I'm now zeroing in on the foundational architecture for this CMS/CRM. React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS seem like a solid tech stack, particularly for a Single Page Application. I'm building out First Timer follow-up and Attendance charts, plus units and events features, alongside a modern "Kingdom Blue" and "Clean White" aesthetic, with a collapsible sidebar and clean cards.


**Detailing the Structure**

My focus is now on the file structure and component breakdown. I've expanded on the pages and components: added a `SuperAdmin.tsx`, expanded upon the role-based UI. I am thinking of using local storage for persistence for a more "production-ready" feel. Additionally, I'm ready to bring in AI integration, using Gemini to suggest follow-up strategies.

### Why Vite?
1. **Architectural Alignment**: Your current code uses a clean, ESM-centric structure (`index.tsx` importing `App.tsx`) and an `importmap`. Vite is built natively on ES modules, making it the most seamless transition from your current setup.
2. **Speed**: Vite offers near-instant Hot Module Replacement (HMR). For a CMS with many modules (Accounting, First Timers, Attendance), this ensures a lightning-fast development experience.

*   Keep your `API_KEY` strictly on the server-side, making it invisible to users.

*   **Go with Vite** if you want the fastest path to deployment and a simple, lightweight SPA that matches your current logic.
